keyFindings.description: spawnRoot's new awaitClosingTrees can await the close that is running it: closeTreeLocked(T) -> releaseSlot(T) (:1821) -> beginPromotionSweep -> advancePromotionSweep -> await startRoot(next) (:2909) -> spawnRoot(next) -> awaitClosingTrees(next) -> await closingTrees.get(T), the same close's promise (closeTree deletes it only in .finally). Reachable when next is a child of T holding its own queued tree record (moved to todo while T lingered; first launch failed so spawnRoot's catch left it queued with a free slot) and T is re-admitted mid-close (the fifth new test's case). Reproduced on a scratch copy: closeTree never settles (timeout 5 s; record closed, child active, wait line logged, 0 provisioning commands); identical test with only the awaitClosingTrees line removed settles in 0.4 s with 12 provisioning commands. Effects: close never settles, isTreeGone(T) true for the daemon's lifetime, both spawns hang, promotionSweep.inFlight never returns to 0, drainSpawns()/stop() hang. Fix: never run the promotion cascade from inside a frame closingTrees still names (closeTreeLocked splices admission.active itself and closeTree kicks beginPromotionSweep after closingTrees.delete in .finally; or advancePromotionSweep skips a candidate whose parent chain names a closing tree and closeTree's .finally re-sweeps), plus the fake-runtime regression for this shape.

The `// Negative wait:` marker is the first of three comment lines, not the line directly above flushEventLoop(50) — the audit-miss shape docs/solutions/testing/await-the-event-not-a-tick-budget.md flags. The drain itself is a correct negative wait.

The bullet quotes the `kept every workspace ...` line without the code's trailing ` (re-admitted while closing)` (processes.ts:3071). Quote the suffix or drop the parenthetical from the code (smaller; also removes a guess, since a `dead` record from a racing resurrection gets the same text).

`Until LEGION-84 lands` is stale: LEGION-84 is on main and provisionIssueWorkspace writes git.abandon-unreachable-commits=false before every fetch (workspace.ts:386-405); the new tests' own `jj config set` (workspace.test.ts:1628) is therefore redundant (harmless).
